title: Nonnegativity of conditional query cost
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty input alphabet, let $\alpha$ be an output type with decidable equality, and let $f:\Omega^n\to\alpha$. For a randomized decision tree that computes $f$, the maximum, over inputs $x$ with $f(x)=a$, of its expected number of queries (with value $0$ assigned when $f(x)\ne a$) is nonnegative for every output $a\in\alpha$.
